title_en: Big data: Hadoop (HDFS, YARN, MapReduce) and Spark (laziness, stages, partitions, shuffle, skew, PySpark)

sentences.ar: في شرحنا ومراجعتنا للمصادر دي النهاردة هنقف قدام لغز تكنولوجي كلنا بنعيشه
sentences.en: In today's review of the sources we face a technological puzzle we all live with.

sentences.ar: إيه اللي بيحصل بجد لما حجم البيانات ينفجر لدرجة إن مستحيل أي جهاز كمبيوتر لوحده مهما كان قوي أو متطور يقدر يستوعبها أو يعالجها
sentences.en: What really happens when data volume explodes so far that no single computer, however powerful or advanced, can hold or process it?

sentences.ar: هنا بالضبط بنلاقي نفسنا مضطرين نسيب فكرة الجهاز السوبر ونروح لفكرة الأنظمة الموزعة أو distributed approach
sentences.en: This is exactly where we must leave the idea of one super machine and move to distributed systems, the distributed approach.

sentences.ar: دعونا نشوف التكنولوجيا دي إزاي كبرت واتطورت عشان تحل الأزمة دي
sentences.en: Let's see how this technology grew and evolved to solve this crisis.

sentences.ar: وعلشان نلتبق أفكارنا دي النقطة الأساسية اللي هنمشي عليها
sentences.en: To organise our thoughts, this is the main outline we will follow.

sentences.ar: هنبدأ بعصر big data
sentences.en: We start with the big data era.

sentences.ar: وبعدين ندخل على الـMapReduce والبيئة بتاعته
sentences.en: Then we move to MapReduce and its ecosystem.

sentences.ar: تالت حاجة هنشوف صورة الـSpark السريعة
sentences.en: Third, we look at the fast Spark revolution.

sentences.ar: ورابعا هنفك طلاصم أزمة الـskew وحلولها
sentences.en: Fourth, we unravel the skew problem and its solutions.

sentences.ar: وأخيرا هنختم بالتطبيق العملي بـPySpark
sentences.en: Finally we close with hands-on practice in PySpark.

sentences.ar: أول حاجة عصر big data
sentences.en: First, the big data era.

sentences.ar: اللحظة اللي الداتا كسرت فيها كل الحدود
sentences.en: The moment when data broke every limit.

sentences.ar: القصة كلها بدأت من اللحظة اللي جهاز واحد رفع فيها الرايا البيضة قدام حجم الداتا
sentences.en: The whole story began the moment a single machine raised the white flag in front of the volume of data.

sentences.ar: لو رجعنا لـ2004 Google كانوا أول ناس يخبطوا في الحيطة دي
sentences.en: Going back to 2004, Google were the first people to hit this wall.

sentences.ar: ونشروا أبحاثهم عن GFS وMapReduce
sentences.en: They published their papers on GFS and MapReduce.

sentences.ar: بعدها بسنتين في 2006 Doug Cutting أخد الأبحاث دي وطلع لنا بـHadoop
sentences.en: Two years later, in 2006, Doug Cutting took those papers and produced Hadoop for us.

sentences.ar: وفضل التطور شغال لحد ما وصلنا لـ2009
sentences.en: And development kept going until we reached 2009.

sentences.ar: لما جمعت Berkeley فجرت صورة Spark عشان تخلي الشغل أسرع بكتير وبطريقة مختلفة
sentences.en: When Berkeley set off the Spark revolution to make work much faster and in a different way.

sentences.ar: تخيلوا معايا كده المشهد ده وكأنه 3D قدامنا
sentences.en: Imagine this scene with me as if it were in 3D in front of us.

sentences.ar: كل حتة أو block حجمه 128 MB بالظبط
sentences.en: Each piece, or block, is exactly 128 MB in size.

sentences.ar: الـblocks دي بتطير حرفياً في الـcluster
sentences.en: These blocks literally fly across the cluster.

sentences.ar: وترشق في أجهزة اسمها DataNodes
sentences.en: And get lodged into machines called DataNodes.

sentences.ar: وعشان نضمن إن ما فيش حاجة تضيع كل block بيتنسخ 3 مرات
sentences.en: And to make sure nothing gets lost, each block is copied 3 times.

sentences.ar: يعني لو عندنا ملف 1 GB هيتكسر لـ 8 blocks
sentences.en: So if we have a 1 GB file, it will be broken into 8 blocks.

sentences.ar: وكل واحد ليه 3 نسخ يعني 24 نسخة متأمنين تماما
sentences.en: And each one has 3 copies, so that is 24 copies, fully protected.

sentences.ar: طب مين اللي سايق الليلة دي وعارف أماكن اللي 24 نسخة
sentences.en: So who is driving this show, and knows the locations of those 24 copies?

sentences.ar: المايسترو هنا اسمه الـNameNode ده اللي مسك خريطة الـcluster كلها وحطتها في الـmemory عنده metadata
sentences.en: The maestro here is called the NameNode; it holds the map of the whole cluster and keeps it in memory, as metadata.

sentences.ar: بس اخدوا بالكم من تفصيلها مهمة جدا
sentences.en: But pay attention to this detail, it is very important.

sentences.ar: ومن هنا بتيجي اهمية ان دايما يكون فيه high availability backup او بديل جاهز يدخل مكانه في جزء من الثانية
sentences.en: From here comes the importance of always having a high availability backup or a ready replacement that steps in within a fraction of a second.

sentences.ar: طب نتخيل سيناريو مرعب شوية
sentences.en: Let's imagine a slightly scary scenario.

sentences.ar: فجأة واحد من الـDataNodes دي مات والنبض او الheartbeat بتاعه وقف
sentences.en: Suddenly one of these DataNodes dies, and its heartbeat stops.

sentences.ar: بعد 10 دقايق و30 ثانية بالزبط الـcluster بياخد باله
sentences.en: After exactly 10 minutes and 30 seconds, the cluster notices.

sentences.ar: هل الدنيا بتوقف؟ خالص
sentences.en: Does everything stop? Not at all.

sentences.ar: فيه هدوء تام الـcluster بيبدأ ينسخ الـblocks اللي وعد دي من الاجهزة التانية السليمة
sentences.en: There is total calm; the cluster starts copying the lost blocks from the other healthy machines.

sentences.ar: والمزهل ان الملف بيفضل يتقري عادي جدا ولا كأن في حاجة حصلت
sentences.en: And the amazing part is that the file keeps being read perfectly normally, as if nothing happened.

sentences.ar: كل اللي بيحصل إن النظام بيدخل في الـsafe mode بيقفل بس كتابة مؤقتا لحد ما يتأكد إن كل حاجة رجعت لمستوى الأمان المطلوب
sentences.en: All that happens is the system enters safe mode, which only blocks writing temporarily until it confirms everything is back to the required safety level.

sentences.ar: ندخل بقى على القسم الثاني الـMapReduce والبيئة المحيطة
sentences.en: Let's move on to the second section: MapReduce and the surrounding ecosystem.

sentences.ar: الفكرة العبقرية إننا نودي الحساب لمكان الداتا مش العكس
sentences.en: The brilliant idea is that we send the computation to where the data is, not the other way round.

sentences.ar: الخطوات بسيطة جداً بس عبقرية
sentences.en: The steps are very simple, yet brilliant.

sentences.ar: بعدين بتيجي أتأل مرحلة الـshuffle
sentences.en: Then comes the heaviest stage, the shuffle.

sentences.ar: تخيلوها كأنها شبكة عن كبوتية ضخمة منورة وصلة بين كل الأجهزة وفيها عدات bytes عمالي عد بجنون
sentences.en: Picture it as a huge spider-web network linking all the machines, with bytes counters ticking up like crazy.

sentences.ar: دي اللحظة اللي الداتا بتسافر فيها عبر الشبكة عشان تتجمع
sentences.en: This is the moment when the data travels across the network to be gathered.

sentences.ar: المرحلة دي غالية جداً وبطيئة
sentences.en: This stage is very expensive and slow.

sentences.ar: ومع الوقت التكنولوجيا دي بنت حواليها نظام بيئي كامل
sentences.en: Over time this technology built a whole ecosystem around itself.

sentences.ar: مثلا Hive جاب لغة الـ SQL السهلة وطبقها على ملفات HDFS ولسه شغال لحد النهاردة
sentences.en: For example Hive brought the easy SQL language and applied it to HDFS files, and it is still working today.

sentences.ar: HBase اتعمل مخصوص للقراءة والكتابة العشوائية طلقة
sentences.en: HBase was built specifically for fast random reads and writes.

sentences.ar: وعندنا ZooKeeper وده زي الحكم اللي بينظم الشغل وبيختار القائد بين الأجهزة ووجوده لسه أساسي
sentences.en: And we have ZooKeeper, which is like the referee that organises the work and picks the leader among machines, and its presence is still essential.

sentences.ar: أما حاجات زي Sqoop وFlume اللي كانوا بينقلوا الداتا فدول بقوا مجرد تاريخ وتراص
sentences.en: As for things like Sqoop and Flume that used to move data, those have become just history and heritage.

sentences.ar: لأن ظهر بعضهم أدوات أحدث قامت بالواجب وزيادة
sentences.en: Because newer tools appeared that did the job and more.

sentences.ar: لو حبينا نجرب الكلام ده عملي على جهازنا الموضوع بيحتاج شوية تصبيطات
sentences.en: If we want to try this hands-on on our own machine, it needs a few set-up steps.

sentences.ar: Java وإعداد SSH و4 ملفات config صغيرة
sentences.en: Java and an SSH setup, and four small config files.

sentences.ar: التركال وحيدة المهمة هي أننا بنعمل format للـNameNode مرة واحدة بس في العمر
sentences.en: The only important point is that we run format on the NameNode once only in a lifetime.

sentences.ar: بعدها بنقوم الـdaemons ونشيك أن الـports فتحة زي 9870 للHDFS و8088 لـYARN
sentences.en: After that we start the daemons and check the ports are open, like 9870 for HDFS and 8088 for YARN.

sentences.ar: وصلنا للقسم الثالث فورة الـSpark السريعة إزاي الـmemory غيرت اللعبة
sentences.en: We have reached the third section, the fast Spark revolution: how memory changed the game.

sentences.ar: اللي Spark بقى دخل قلب الموازين
sentences.en: Spark came along and turned the balance upside down.

sentences.ar: هو ما غيرش المفاهيم الأساسية بس غير طريقة التنفيذ 180 درجة
sentences.en: It did not change the basic concepts but changed the way of execution by 180 degrees.

sentences.ar: لو بصينا على المقارنة هنلاقي الـMapReduce كانت إيه القوي بيقرأ ويكتب من الـdisk بعد كل خطوة
sentences.en: If we look at the comparison we find MapReduce reads and writes from the disk after every step.

sentences.ar: Spark قال لأ أنا هحتفظ بالبيانات في الذاكرة أو الـmemory
sentences.en: Spark said no: I will keep the data in memory.

sentences.ar: ودخل لقى أطير وأسرع لحد 100 مرة
sentences.en: And it turned out faster, up to 100 times.

sentences.ar: وكمان بيدعم لغات كتير زي Python وSQL
sentences.en: It also supports many languages like Python and SQL.

sentences.ar: الفجرة أنهم مش بينفسوا بعض في الغالب تلاقيهم شغالين مع بعض
sentences.en: The surprise is that they do not compete with each other; mostly you find them working together.

sentences.ar: Hadoop يشير ويخزن الداتا وSpark يقوم بالمعالجة الصاروخية
sentences.en: Hadoop holds and stores the data, and Spark does the rocket-fast processing.

sentences.ar: ونقعد نبني الخريطة بتاعته أو الـDAG من جوه
sentences.en: And keep building its map, the DAG, from the inside.

sentences.ar: وهو قاعد يتفرج وما فيش أي حاجة بتحصل حرفيا زيرو تنفيذ
sentences.en: While it just sits watching and nothing at all happens, literally zero execution.

sentences.ar: وبعدين ينفجر ويبدأ يشتغل في ثواني
sentences.en: Then it explodes into action and gets going within seconds.

sentences.ar: العمليات الخفيفة أو الـnarrow زي الفلطرة مثلا دي بتفضل وتتعمل في مكانها على نفس الجهاز
sentences.en: The light, narrow operations like filtering stay and run in place on the same machine.

sentences.ar: السر مش إننا نحفظ أسماء العمليات
sentences.en: The secret is not memorising the names of operations.

sentences.ar: السر إننا ندور على الـExchange أو الـshuffle ونعرف هو بيحصل ليه
sentences.en: The secret is to look for the Exchange, the shuffle, and understand why it happens.

sentences.ar: وهنا لازم ندي تحية للـCatalyst Optimizer العقل المدبر اللي بيعيد كتابة الكود بتاعنا عشان يفلطر الداتا بدري بدري
sentences.en: And here we must salute the Catalyst Optimizer, the mastermind that rewrites our code so it filters the data early on.

sentences.ar: وده اللي بيخلي استخدام الـ DataFrames أحسن وأسرع بكتير جداً من الـ RDDs بتاعت زمان
sentences.en: That is what makes using DataFrames much, much better and faster than the old-days RDDs.

sentences.ar: كل ده بيرجعنا لنقطة محورية الـ Partition
sentences.en: All of this brings us back to a pivotal point, the partition.

sentences.ar: تصبيت العدد ده هو اللي بيفتح الباب للسرعة الحقيقية
sentences.en: Getting this number right is what opens the door to real speed.

sentences.ar: ندخل على القسم الرابع أزمة الـskew وحلولها
sentences.en: We move on to the fourth section: the skew problem and its solutions.

sentences.ar: المشكلة اللي بتجنن أي حد شغال في الـbig data اخيالوا معايا الموقف المستفز ده
sentences.en: The problem that drives crazy anyone working in big data - imagine this infuriating situation with me.

sentences.ar: طيب نحل لها إزاي؟
sentences.en: So how do we solve it?

sentences.ar: المصادر بتطرح 3 حلول سحرية للمشكلة دي
sentences.en: The sources put forward 3 magic solutions to this problem.

sentences.ar: التاني حاجة اسمها Salting يعني بنمسك الـkey اللي عامل الزحمة دي ونلزق فيه لاحقة عشوائية عشان نفتته ونقسمه
sentences.en: The second is called Salting: we take the key causing the congestion and glue a random suffix onto it to break it up and split it.

sentences.ar: والحل الثالث هو الـbroadcast join
sentences.en: The third solution is the broadcast join.

sentences.ar: وأخيراً القسم الخامس التطبيق العملي بـPySpark
sentences.en: And finally the fifth section: hands-on practice in PySpark.

sentences.ar: إزاي نترجم كل الكلام ده لكود حقيقي
sentences.en: How do we translate all this talk into real code?

sentences.ar: في شوية قواعد ذهبية كده عشان نكتب كود نظيف وسريع
sentences.en: There are a few golden rules so that we write clean and fast code.

sentences.ar: دايماً حديدوا الـschema بإيديكم بـ StructType بدل ما تسيبه Spark يخمنها ويضايع وقتنا
sentences.en: Always define the schema yourselves with StructType instead of leaving Spark to guess it and waste our time.

sentences.ar: تاني حاجة خلوا دايما الـ Parquet هو صيغة التخزين الأساسية بتاعتكم لأنه زاكي وموفر وسريع
sentences.en: Second, always make Parquet your basic storage format, because it is smart, space-saving and fast.

sentences.ar: وتالت وأهم حاجة استخدموا الـ Built-in Functions بتاعة Spark
sentences.en: And third, and most important, use the built-in functions of Spark.

sentences.ar: وتجنبوا تماما الـ Python UDFs لأنها حرفيا بتدمر الأداء وبتخليه بطيء جدا
sentences.en: And completely avoid Python UDFs, because they literally destroy performance and make it very slow.

sentences.ar: ولما نحب نعمل شغل متقدم الـ Window Functions بتخلص لنا حسابات معقدة
sentences.en: And when we want to do advanced work, Window Functions finish complex calculations for us.

sentences.ar: زي المجميع التراكمية أو الـ Running Totals والـranking بسهولة
sentences.en: Like cumulative sums or running totals, and ranking, with ease.

sentences.ar: والتريكة اللي بتفرق بجد هي لما نيجي نكتب النتائج
sentences.en: And the trick that really makes a difference is when we come to write the results.

sentences.ar: استخدموا Partition By وحطوا جواها مثلاً Order Date الحركة دي سحر
sentences.en: Use Partition By and put inside it, say, Order Date - this move is magic.

sentences.ar: لأنها بتقسم الملفات بالتاريخ فأي استعلام أو Query بعد كده بيحتاج داتا يوم معين
sentences.en: Because it splits the files by date, so any query afterwards that needs the data of a certain day.

sentences.ar: هيروح يقرأ ملفات اليوم ده بس ويتجاهل الباقي تماماً فسرعة الاستعلام بتبقى خيالية
sentences.en: Will go and read that day's files only and ignore the rest entirely, so query speed becomes amazing.

sentences.ar: كل التفاصيل اللي اتكلمنا فيها دي في الآخر بتتجمع عشان تطلع لنا Daily PySpark Job قوي وموصوق
sentences.en: All the details we discussed finally come together to give us a strong and reliable Daily PySpark Job.

sentences.ar: بيقرأ Partition 1 يحسب تأسيمات العملاء زي الVIP والـGold ويكتب مؤشرات الأداء أو الKPIs بتاعة اليوم ده بس
sentences.en: It reads one partition, calculates customer segments like VIP and Gold, and writes the KPIs for just that day.

sentences.ar: ده بيعتبر التطبيق العملي المثالي لكل مفاهيم التغزين والمعالجة الموزعة اللي فصصناها النهاردة
sentences.en: This counts as the ideal hands-on application of all the distributed storage and processing concepts we dissected today.

sentences.ar: بس قبل ما نختم فيه سؤال بيطرح نفسه بقوة
sentences.en: But before we wrap up, a question forces itself on us strongly.

sentences.ar: احنا كل ده عملين نتكلم عن الـbatch processing أو معالجة الداتا بعد ما تتخزن وتجمع
sentences.en: All along we have been talking about batch processing, meaning processing data after it has been stored and gathered.

sentences.ar: بس في عصرنا السريع ده الداتا ما بتستناش حد
sentences.en: But in our fast era, data does not wait for anyone.

sentences.ar: طيب إيه اللي بيحصل لما نكون محتاجين نعرف المعلومة في نفس اللحظة من خلال الـreal-time streaming مع أدوات زي Kafka
sentences.en: So what happens when we need to know the information at that very moment, through real-time streaming with tools like Kafka?

sentences.ar: ده بقى اللغز الجديد اللي محتاجين نفكر فيه ونتعلمه المرة الجاية
sentences.en: That is the new puzzle we need to think about and learn next time.

sentences.ar: أتمنى تكونوا استفدتوا من تحليلنا للمصادر دي النهاردة
sentences.en: I hope you benefited from our analysis of these sources today.

sentences.ar: وتكون فكرة الأنظمة الموزعة بقت أوضح وممتعة أكتر
sentences.en: And that the idea of distributed systems has become clearer and more enjoyable.

facts.rule: A number goes on screen with its fact id as `ref`/`data_refs`. `unmatched_numbers` are spoken but have no data-contract fact: their source is the sentence itself (a valid `s:` ref); never replace them with a different figure.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.

first_mention_gloss.gloss_ar: إن key واحد شايل أغلب الداتا

glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

concepts.def_en: Data too large or fast to store or process on a single machine, so it is split and processed across a cluster.
concepts.failure: Calling any large file big data; if one machine can handle it, it is not.

concepts.def_en: A distributed processing model: map transforms records into key-value pairs, shuffle groups them by key, reduce aggregates each group.
concepts.failure: Overlooking that the shuffle between map and reduce, not the compute, dominates runtime.

concepts.def_en: Apache Spark: a distributed engine that processes large datasets in parallel across a cluster, keeping data in memory where possible.
concepts.failure: Using Spark for small data, where cluster overhead outweighs any speed gain.

concepts.def_en: Uneven distribution where one key holds most of the data, so one partition's task runs far longer than the rest.
concepts.failure: Adding executors to fix it; the one hot key still lands on one task.

concepts.def_en: An open-source framework that stores huge data across many machines with HDFS and processes it in parallel, originally with MapReduce.
concepts.failure: Using Hadoop for small data; its overhead only pays off at large scale.

concepts.def_en: The HDFS master that holds the cluster's map in memory (which block lives on which DataNode) but never stores the file data itself.
concepts.failure: Thinking the NameNode stores file data; it holds only the map to the blocks.

concepts.def_en: Data about data: schemas, locations, sizes and state that describe and track the actual data without containing it.
concepts.failure: Treating metadata loss as harmless; without the map, intact data is unreadable.

concepts.def_en: Redistributing data across machines over the network so rows with the same key land together; the heaviest, costliest step in distributed jobs.
concepts.failure: Treating shuffle as free; it moves data over the network and dominates job time.

concepts.def_en: Structured Query Language: the standard declarative language for querying and changing data in relational databases by describing what you want.
concepts.failure: Thinking SQL runs in written order; the engine plans execution in its own order.

concepts.def_en: Hadoop Distributed File System: splits files into blocks spread across DataNodes and keeps several replicas of each on different machines.
concepts.failure: Storing huge numbers of tiny files, which overload the NameNode's metadata memory.

concepts.def_en: A statically typed, object-oriented language that runs on the JVM; used for large backend systems, APIs and big-data tooling.
concepts.failure: Ignoring null handling, leading to NullPointerException at runtime.

concepts.def_en: Secure Shell: an encrypted protocol for logging into and running commands on a remote machine, usually with key pairs.
concepts.failure: Chasing network causes when SSH refuses entry because key file permissions are too open.

concepts.def_en: Hadoop's resource manager that allocates cluster CPU and memory to jobs, so no single job monopolises the cluster.
concepts.failure: Confusing YARN with a storage layer; it schedules resources and never stores data.

concepts.def_en: Persistent storage, far slower than RAM, that keeps data after power-off; when full, everything else starts failing strangely.
concepts.failure: Ignoring disk usage until it fills and unrelated services begin failing with strange errors.

concepts.def_en: A readable, general-purpose programming language widely used for data analysis, automation, pipelines and AI work.
concepts.failure: Using plain loops over huge data instead of vectorized pandas or SQL operations.

concepts.def_en: A slice of data split by key or range, so work touches only part of it; in window functions, the rows one calculation sees.
concepts.failure: Choosing a partition key queries never filter on, so nothing is pruned.

concepts.def_en: Adding a random suffix to a hot key so its rows spread across several partitions, fixing data skew in joins and aggregations.
concepts.failure: Salting one side only; the other side must be expanded to match every salt.

concepts.def_en: A join that copies the small table to every node, so the large table is joined locally with no shuffle.
concepts.failure: Broadcasting a table too big for executor memory, causing out-of-memory failures.

concepts.def_en: Combines rows from two tables by matching key columns, such as orders with their customers.
concepts.failure: Joining on a non-unique key silently multiplies rows and inflates totals.

concepts.def_en: The declared structure of data: field or column names, types and constraints, which a table or message must follow.
concepts.failure: Changing a field's type or removing it without checking that downstream consumers still work.

concepts.def_en: A columnar, compressed, open file format for analytics: queries read only the columns they need, saving space and I/O.
concepts.failure: Writing many tiny Parquet files, which causes the small-files problem.

concepts.def_en: A request to a database or search system to fetch, filter or change data; in SQL, usually a SELECT statement.
concepts.failure: Blaming hardware for a slow query when a full table scan is the cause.

concepts.def_en: A group of records processed together in one run, as opposed to streaming; a batch identifier makes reloads safe to repeat.
concepts.failure: Rerunning a batch load without deleting that batch first, duplicating rows.

concepts.def_en: A distributed, append-only event log: producers write events to topics, consumers read forward, and events are retained for a set window.
concepts.failure: Treating Kafka as a database with a different name; it is a log with retention.

concepts.def_en: Processing data continuously as events arrive, instead of waiting to process it in periodic batches.
concepts.failure: Assuming events arrive on time and in order; late data breaks results.
